    • getType

      public PbcsMemberType getType()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Gets the member type, corresponding to the known planning member types, such as Scenario or Account. If the type is not known (to the enum) then PbcsMemberType.UNKNOWN will be returned. If you need to parse some specific [but unknown] member type not represented in the enum, then use the PbcsMember.getObjectNumericType() method.
      Specified by:
      getType in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      the member type (if known)

    • getAlias

      public String getAlias()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      The alias for this member. Although EPM cloud supports alias tables, the aliases don't seem to surface in the REST endpoint for fetching member information. The alias you get here is the "default" alias that comes back as a single property from the member info endpoint.
      Specified by:
      getAlias in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      the member alias

    • getOldName

      public String getOldName()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Gets the "old name" for this member. I'm not sure how this is used, but it is a property that gets returned from the member info endpoint. I don't believe I have seen a value different from the actual member name.
      Specified by:
      getOldName in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      the "old name" for this member

    • getParent

      public PbcsApplication getParent()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Gets the parent of this member object, which is currently the containing application. If you want to parent member, consider using PbcsMember.getParentName() or PbcsMember.getParentMember(). This method is named as such because it is a standard aspect of the PbcsObject interface.
      Specified by:
      getParent in interface PbcsMember
      Specified by:
      getParent in interface PbcsObject
      Returns:

    • getParentMember

      public PbcsMember getParentMember()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Gets the parent of this member. For most members, this value will already exist, but calling this may cause a member lookup to happen. If you just need the name of the parent, then using PbcsMember.getParentName() is guaranteed to return without making an additional request to the server.
      Specified by:
      getParentMember in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      the parent of this member, null if there isn't one (e.g., it's a dimension root)

    • getDataStorage

      public String getDataStorage()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember

      Specified by:
      getDataStorage in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:

    • getLevel

      public int getLevel()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Gets the calculated level of the member. The level appears to come back in the member info payload; however, it always has a value of 0. I believe this is an oversight on Oracle's part. Note: shared members will return the level of the shared member, not the prototype member. In other words, shared members will always have a level of 0 (since shared members cannot have children).
      Specified by:
      getLevel in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      the calculated level of this member

    • getGeneration

      public int getGeneration()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Generation of the member. Tops of dimensions are, by definition, generation 1. The "outline itself" is considered to be generation 0 (philosophically).
      Specified by:
      getGeneration in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      the generation of the member (1 for dimension, 2 for child of dimension, and so on)

    • isLeaf

      public boolean isLeaf()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsMember
      Convenience method that checks whether the given member is a leaf node (level-0) or not. Effectively this should always be true in the case that getChildren().size() == 0. This should also be true in case getChildren() returns null, although valid implementations of this interface should return an empty collection instead of null.
      Specified by:
      isLeaf in interface PbcsMember
      Returns:
      true if this member has no children and is a level-0/leaf node, false otherwise.
